record.original_question: Let n >= 2 and let C:[0,1]^n -> [0,1] be an n-ary copula, meaning that C is n-increasing and satisfies the usual copula boundary conditions. Define C_1 by C_1(x_1,...,x_n)=C(x_1,...,x_n)-product_{i=1}^n (x_i-C(x_1,...,x_n)). Is C_1 always n-increasing, and hence itself an n-ary copula? If not, characterize those n-ary copulas C for which C_1 is again an n-ary copula.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1 (Mesiar). Let C : [0, 1]^n -> [0, 1] be an n-ary copula. Define C1 : [0, 1]^n -> [0, 1] by C1(x1,...,xn) = C(x1,...,xn) - product_{i=1}^n (xi - C(x1,...,xn)). Is the function C1 n-increasing, i.e., is it an n-copula? If in general not, characterize all n-copulas C such that C1 is an n-copula, too.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \ge 2$. A function $C:[0,1]^n \to [0,1]$ is called an $n$-ary copula if:
(i) $C(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=0$ whenever $x_i=0$ for some $i$;
(ii) $C(1,\ldots,1,x_i,1,\ldots,1)=x_i$ for every $i$ and every $x_i\in[0,1]$;
(iii) $C$ is $n$-increasing, i.e., for every $n$-dimensional box $\prod_{i=1}^n[a_i,b_i]\subseteq[0,1]^n$ the $C$-volume
$$V_C\!\left(\prod_{i=1}^n[a_i,b_i]\right)=\sum_{(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_n)\in\{0,1\}^n}(-1)^{n-\sum_i\varepsilon_i}\,C(c_1^{\varepsilon_1},\ldots,c_n^{\varepsilon_n})$$
with $c_i^0=a_i$ and $c_i^1=b_i$, is nonnegative.

Given an $n$-ary copula $C$, define $C_1:[0,1]^n\to[0,1]$ by
$$C_1(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=C(x_1,\ldots,x_n)-\prod_{i=1}^n\bigl(x_i-C(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\bigr).$$

Is $C_1$ always $n$-increasing, and hence itself an $n$-ary copula? If not, give a complete characterization of those $n$-ary copulas $C$ for which $C_1$ is again an $n$-ary copula.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface related literature on perturbations and transformations of copulas (Klement–Mesiar–Pap; later work on perturbation-based copulas through 2021–2024), but no source was found that directly resolves or characterizes the specific transformation $C_1(x)=C(x)-\prod_i(x_i-C(x))$ in the $n$-ary case. Status could not be verified.
